classification.difficultyReason: Interpret equal-edge marks, subtract the wall height from the total height, split the tent ends into rectangles and triangles, and convert the complete canvas area into cost.

content.prompt: The floor, sides and roof of this tent are made from canvas at a cost of $\$5$ per square metre. The tent’s dimensions are shown in the diagram. What is the cost of the canvas for the tent?

spec.description: House-shaped pentagonal prism, extruded upwards and right, with double equality ticks on all five front edges and an external total-height arrow. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in black.
spec.mathematics: Front width 1.5 m; all five front boundary edges are marked equal; overall height 2.8 m; prism length 2 m. The decimal dimensions are treated as the supplied measurements.

answer.worked:
The equal-edge marks give wall height and roof slope length $1.5\,\mathrm m$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Triangle height}&=2.8-1.5=1.3\,\mathrm m\\
\text{Two triangular ends}&=2\times\frac12\times1.5\times1.3=1.95\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Two rectangular ends}&=2\times1.5\times1.5=4.5\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Two side walls}&=2\times1.5\times2=6\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Two roof rectangles}&=2\times1.5\times2=6\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Floor}&=1.5\times2=3\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Surface area}&=1.95+4.5+6+6+3=21.45\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Cost}&=21.45\times\$5=\$107.25
\end{align*}$$
